mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Limited Partnership Registration Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: APOSTILLE PATH (Convention state): certify at Hong Kong Notary Public, then obtain an Apostille from the High Court of Hong Kong. CONSULAR PATH (non-Convention state): certify at Hong Kong Notary Public, then legalize at the Consulate/Embassy of the destination state. The two paths are mutually exclusive and never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Continuing Registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: APOSTILLE PATH: notarized copy issued by Companies Registry, then Apostille by the High Court of Hong Kong. CONSULAR PATH: notarized copy then consular legalization at the destination state's mission. Choose only one path.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney of the General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General Partner's board or sole corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: APOSTILLE PATH: notarized resolution/POA signed by authorized directors, then Apostille by the High Court of Hong Kong or relevant mainland Chinese competent authority if executed in China. CONSULAR PATH: notarized then legalized at the destination embassy/consulate. Never use both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: All partners under the Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 37)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: APOSTILLE PATH: execute deed before a Hong Kong notary, apostille by the High Court of Hong Kong. CONSULAR PATH: notarize before notary public, then consular legalization at the destination state's consulate. Parallel paths, not sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Investor's onboarding corporate bank (e.g., HSBC or international bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: APOSTILLE PATH: bank officer countersignature notarized by a notary public, Apostille issued by the competent authority of the bank's jurisdiction. CONSULAR PATH: notarized bank reference letter legalized by the destination state's consulate. Either path only.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Incumbency and Compliance Certificate for Corporate Investor / UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Mainland Chinese SAMR registry or Hong Kong Companies Registry as applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: APOSTILLE PATH: certified extract notarized locally, Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the PRC (for mainland documents) or High Court of Hong Kong (for HK documents). CONSULAR PATH: notarized extract then legalization at the destination state's consulate. Mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All general partners, limited partners, and every individual holding at least 25% of the FIP must undergo independent PEP and sanctions screening at formation and continuing on a 30-day cycle. Databases to be queried include OFAC SDN list, United Nations Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated financial sanctions, UK OFSI list, Hong Kong Monetary Authority AML/CFT circular reminders, China's PRC sanctions and SAMR public administrative penalty database, and the World Bank debarment list. Adverse hits trigger automatic escalation to a senior compliance officer, enhanced due diligence under Cap. 615, documentary verification of source of funds, and possible notification to the Companies Registry and the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit. The screening outcome must be dated and archived with the partnership book.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry Integrated Companies Registry System (ICRIS) Cyber Search Centre and e-Registration Portal for Limited Partnerships
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Hong Kong foreign-invested limited partnership name may be in English, Traditional Chinese, or both. The English name must terminate with 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.'; the Chinese name must end with '有限合夥' (Traditional Chinese characters, not simplified). A phonetic transliteration in Mandarin/Putonghua is accepted if the English registered name is concurrently adopted. The four-tier naming convention requires (1) a distinctive element, (2) a true business activity descriptor, (3) the legal form suffix, and (4) an optional territorial indicator or trade mark, in that strict order. The Companies Registry will reject any name that is identical or confusingly similar to an existing entity, or that contains obscene, offensive, or forbidden tokens.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where the Registrar refuses a proposed name, the applicant may file a written appeal with the Hong Kong Companies Registry within 14 days after the refusal notice, relying on section 100(4) of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) as applied to limited partnerships. The appeal must state the grounds in law and fact, provide a certified search report from the trade marks registry, explain the phonetic and cultural distinctiveness of the proposed denomination, and request withdrawal or substitution if similarity is admitted. If the appeal fails, the applicant may apply for judicial review to the Court of First Instance and simultaneously submit a fresh name for fast-track clearance. Legal fees for the administrative appeal are typically USD 2,000 to USD 5,000 based on market benchmarks.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mailbox addresses are generally rejected by the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department and mainstream banks for this industry. A civil-infrastructure BIM/CAD outsourcing partnership must demonstrate real economic substance to secure bank accounts and wire-transfer/Wise payment rails. The IRD can disregard a sham virtual office under anti-avoidance provisions and may deny interest deduction and treaty benefits; the Companies Registry may penalize a false principal place of business. A serviced office with a genuine lease, nameplate, phone line, and partner/director physical attendance is the minimum acceptable threshold; a shared virtual mail-forwarding service is insufficient for banking onboarding.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) valid executed lease or tenancy agreement for at least 12 months, (2) utility bills and telecom invoices issued in the partnership's name, (3) employee employment contracts and MPF contribution records, (4) letterheads, invoices and contracts showing the registered office address, (5) exterior/interior signage identifying the entity, (6) bank statements from a Hong Kong bank evidencing actual transactions. Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspection by the IRD or Companies Registry is 15-25% within the first year of operations where annual outward remittance exceeds USD 500,000. The risk increases to 60% where the address is in a virtual-office building or a serviced-office complex that the IRD has profiled. Registry and tax field inspections are typically conducted without prior notice under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112) and Companies Ordinance s.357.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap 37), sections 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8; Partnership Ordinance (Cap 38), sections 2 and 3; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap 310), sections 5 and 6; Stamp Duty Ordinance (Cap 117) where applicable; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap 615), Schedule 2, where applicable. The Companies Ordinance (Cap 622) is not the governing statute for a partnership vehicle.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, Limited Partnerships Section, Registrar of Companies, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, with ancillary Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statement of Limited Partnership (Form LP 1) filed under section 5 of the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap 37), together with Application for Business Registration (Form IRBR 193) under section 5 of the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap 310).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a limited partnership under Cap 37 or a general partnership under Cap 38. The Partnership Agreement governs the amount, timing, form and conditions of capital contributions. No blocked escrow account is required under Hong Kong legislation; however, if a China-based partner remits contributions, such remittance must first satisfy applicable PRC outbound investment (NDRC), Ministry of Commerce filing, and SAFE foreign exchange registration, and funds should only be deposited into the partnership bank account after that account is lawfully opened and operated under the banking mandate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA RESOLUTION OF THE MANAGEMENT BOARD OF [FOREIGN-INVESTED PARTNERSHIP] (A HONG KONG LIMITED PARTNERSHIP PROPOSED TO BE REGISTERED UNDER THE LIMITED PARTNERSHIPS ORDINANCE (CAP 37)). WHEREAS, the Partnership is about to be registered as a limited partnership with the Companies Registry of Hong Kong SAR; and WHEREAS, the general partner has prepared a draft Limited Partnership Agreement, selected a registered office at [address], selected [Bank] as the intended principal banker, and identified the statutory officers; and WHEREAS, the Management Board has considered and resolved to adopt all necessary corporate governance arrangements in accordance with the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap 37), the Partnership Ordinance (Cap 38), the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap 310) and the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap 615); NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS RESOLVED unanimously as follows: 1. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Partnership shall be at [address] in Hong Kong, and the General Partner is authorized and directed to file the Statement of Limited Partnership, to accept service of legal process, and to file all subsequent notices of change with the Companies Registry. 2. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND CONTRIBUTIONS: RESOLVED, that the capital contribution schedule in Exhibit A to these minutes is approved; no minimum paid-up capital is required by law; each partner's subscription is payable as stated in the Partnership Agreement; no blocked escrow account is required; and contributions from China-based investors shall be remitted only upon completion of applicable outbound investment and foreign exchange registration under PRC law. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the partnership bank account shall be opened with [Bank] Hong Kong branch; the General Partner and the Compliance Officer are authorized to execute account opening forms, banking mandates, indemnities and foreign exchange documents; and all cash withdrawals and outgoing wire instructions above [HKD threshold] shall require two authorized signatories, one of whom must be the Compliance Officer. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed General Partner; [name] is appointed Compliance Officer and Money Laundering Reporting Officer; [name] is appointed Responsible Person for Business Registration and Tax Filings; and [name] is appointed Corporate Administrator responsible for statutory records and filings. 5. GENERAL AUTHORITY AND EFFECTIVENESS: RESOLVED, that the appointed officers be and are hereby authorized to execute applications, deeds, certificates, notices and other documents, to pay all prescribed fees, to engage solicitors and accountants, and to take all steps necessary or desirable to complete the formation of the Partnership, obtain the Business Registration Certificate, and open the bank accounts. This resolution shall be binding on all partners and may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: China Outbound Investment Qualification and Name Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) ODI filing system; Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) or provincial MOFCOM outbound investment window; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) branch for foreign exchange registration; Hong Kong Companies Registry via Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS) for name check.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a legal and know-your-partner due diligence on all Chinese and Hong Kong partners, verify identity, source of funds, and whether the investing partner is a PRC entity or individual subject to ODI filing thresholds. For any PRC enterprise investing in Hong Kong, complete NDRC overseas investment filing or registration under Order No. 11, 2017 and MOFCOM outbound investment filing under Order No. 3, 2018 before any outward remittance, or properly document a legal exemption where the transaction is non-qualifying. Use ICRIS to verify that the proposed Chinese and English name of the partnership is acceptable and not identical or confusingly similar to an existing Hong Kong corporation, limited company, or limited partnership. Execute the preliminary related-party risk assessment and document the substantive business activities under ISIC 7110 as engineering design, BIM modeling and CAD drafting so that the banking and AML risk classification remains Low Risk Standard.
required_dossiers: Chinese and English partnership name check report from ICRIS
Certified copies of passports of all Chinese and Hong Kong partners
Proof of residential address for each partner issued within the last three months
NDRC overseas investment filing or registration certificate where applicable
MOFCOM outbound investment certificate where applicable
SAFE foreign exchange registration certificate where applicable
Bank reference letter or professional reference letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ICRIS name check indicates a conflict or confusing similarity, amend the proposed name or file a letter of consent from the prior entity. If NDRC or MOFCOM issues a query, file supplemental economic and commercial justification within the statutory response window, normally no longer than ten working days, and re-submit. If SAFE requests additional source of fund documents, provide bank statements, business contracts, and audited financial statements of the investor. An outstanding NDRC verification cannot be ignored and must be resolved by counsel before capital contribution remittance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Stamp Duty Assessment and Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong licensed solicitor or notary public; Stamp Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR, for stamping of any dutiable registered office lease or agreement.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a comprehensive Limited Partnership Agreement under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap 37) and the Partnership Ordinance (Cap 38) containing the firm name, principal place of business, partnership purpose, identified general and limited partners, capital contribution schedule, profit sharing and loss sharing ratio, governance of the management board, banking signatories, admission and withdrawal of partners, indemnification, dissolution, and China investor restrictive covenants. Ensure that the China partner's contribution is expressly characterized as partnership capital, not loan or share capital, so that the pass-through tax classification and partnership limitation of liability are preserved. If the registered office is held under a lease, submit the tenancy document to the Stamp Office for assessment and pay any stamp duty. Execute the agreement before a licensed solicitor or notary public, with each partner certifying capacity and authority, and request certified copies for the later bank and regulatory filings.
required_dossiers: Draft Limited Partnership Agreement
Certificate of incumbency or board resolution for any corporate partner
Notarized power of attorney for each signing officer or partner
Hong Kong office lease or landlord consent letter for the registered office
Stamp duty application form and tenancy agreement if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Stamp Office imposes additional duty or a penalty, pay the assessed amount under protest and file an appeal with the Board of Review within the time prescribed by the Inland Revenue Ordinance. If a partner's signing capacity is questioned, obtain a fresh notarized power of attorney and re-execute all signature pages of the agreement before the same or another notary public.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Limited Partnership with the Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Limited Partnerships Section, Registrar of Companies, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region; online filing through the Companies Registry e-Services where available.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the duly executed Statement of Limited Partnership on Form LP 1 together with the prescribed fee, the registered office consent, and certified copies of the Limited Partnership Agreement if requested. The statement must include the firm name, general nature of business, principal place of business, full names and addresses of all general partners, the fact that the partnership is a limited partnership, and the amount of capital contributed by each limited partner. The General Partner must sign the statement and acknowledge that a false statement may constitute an offence under Cap 37. When the Companies Registry is satisfied, it will issue the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership. The registered office must be a physical address in Hong Kong capable of receiving service of process and must not be a public post office box.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed Form LP 1 Statement of Limited Partnership
Consent to act and address of the registered office in Hong Kong
Certified copy of the executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Photographic identification and proof of residential address for every general and limited partner
Name check report from ICRIS
Prescribed government fee payment voucher
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry issues a requisition or query, respond in writing within fourteen days with a revised Form LP 1, an explanatory cover letter, or a legal opinion on the partnership structure. If the application lapses because no response was submitted, re-file a fresh Form LP 1 and pay any re-submission fee. A person must not carry on business as an unregistered limited partnership because that may expose the limited partner to general liability.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration Certificate with the Inland Revenue Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region; online through the eTAX and e-Business Registration portals.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after the partnership begins operations or immediately after registration, whichever is earlier, apply for the Business Registration Certificate under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap 310). Submit Form IRBR 193 together with the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership, the registered office address, and the prescribed annual fee. State the business nature as engineering design, building information modeling, and CAD drafting consultancy under ISIC 7110 and NAICS 541330. The Business Registration Certificate must be displayed conspicuously at the registered office and renewed annually or triennially. The certificate is a condition precedent to opening a corporate bank account and entering into certain commercial contracts, and it should therefore be obtained before contracting with clients.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership from Companies Registry
Form IRBR 193 Application for Business Registration
Business address in Hong Kong and contact details of the Responsible Person
Identification documents of all partners
Latest address for service if different from the registered office
Payment of the prescribed registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Inland Revenue Department returns the application for correction, amend the particulars and resubmit via the eTAX portal within fourteen days. If a late registration penalty is imposed, file a written mitigation letter explaining the date of commencement and attach evidence of compliance; the Commissioner may reduce or waive the penalty where default is inadvertent and reasonable. If the business registration fee is disputed, pay the assessed amount under protest and apply for a review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, Statutory Records and AML Governance Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong Monetary Authority licensed authorized institution selected by the Partnership; Companies Registry for subsequent changes of registered particulars; Inland Revenue Department for subsequent tax and business registration updates.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the partnership bank account at the appointed bank by presenting the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership, the Business Registration Certificate, the executed Limited Partnership Agreement, the pro-forma resolution of the Management Board authorizing signatories, source of funds statements, and the AML risk assessment. The bank may require a completed account opening application, a corporate structure chart, client contracts, and a forecast of expected transaction volume and counterparty jurisdictions. Implement internal controls for outgoing wire instructions requiring dual signatories above the approved threshold and for segregation of partner capital from client funds if any. Maintain statutory records at the registered office, including the register of general and limited partners, capital contribution ledger, copies of statements and notices filed with the Companies Registry, minutes of Management Board meetings, and correspondence with the Inland Revenue Department. If the Partnership becomes a designated non-financial business under Cap 615, appoint the Money Laundering Reporting Officer and implement a written AML policy.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Business Registration Certificate
Executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Resolution of the Management Board authorizing bank account opening and signatories
Certified passports and proof of address of authorized signatories
Source of wealth and source of funds statements
AML risk assessment and business plan
Lease or ownership title of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues an enhanced due diligence request, provide notarized proof of economic substance, client contracts, invoices, and a projected transaction flow within the bank's stated deadline. If the bank rejects the application, apply to at least two alternative licensed banks rather than litigating, because account opening is within the bank's commercial discretion. If the Companies Registry rejects a subsequent change of registered particulars, file the prescribed amendment form and pay the fee before the statutory deadline and maintain a contemporaneous record of all correspondence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing activity under ISIC 7110; the activity is an office-based professional, scientific and technical service. The only competent authority for business operation is the Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no manufacturing, processing, factory, or warehouse operating license is required for engineering design, BIM modeling, or CAD drafting services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable; if a physical project were later initiated, the relevant authority would be the Environmental Protection Department of Hong Kong SAR under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap 499).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no EIA designated engineering project component under Schedule 2 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap 499) is triggered by an office-based BIM/CAD design consultancy; no land alteration, construction, or discharge activity is proposed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater generation, VOC emission source, point source discharge, hazardous waste generation, or industrial emissions threshold applies to the registered office. General office waste is handled by municipal waste collection; no environmental permit or discharge license is required for the digital services described.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for industrial Civil Defense fire permits because there is no physical manufacturing, dangerous goods storage, or warehousing. The Hong Kong registered office must, however, comply with the Buildings Ordinance (Cap 123) means of escape in case of fire and the Fire Safety (Commercial Premises) Ordinance (Cap 502) if the premises are a commercial office. If employees are engaged, the Partnership must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap 509) and the Employment Ordinance (Cap 57). No Certificate of Fire Safety Installation, Civil Defense certificate, or dangerous goods license is required for the pure digital engineering design activity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region; electronic filing and account administration are conducted via the GovHK eTAX portal (https://www.etax.gov.hk) and the IRD public website (https://www.ird.gov.hk)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) formed in Hong Kong must apply for a Business Registration Certificate under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) using Form IRBR 1 (Application for Business Registration) within one month of the commencement of business. The application is submitted to the Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department and must disclose all individual and corporate partners, including non-resident partners. Upon approval, the IRD issues a Business Registration Certificate bearing a Business Registration Number (BRN), which functions as the Hong Kong Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) for the partnership. If any non-resident partner has no Hong Kong address, a Hong Kong tax representative or authorized representative must be appointed to receive statutory correspondence. The Business Registration Certificate must be renewed annually or triennially according to the prescribed issuance cycle. For profits tax purposes, the partnership itself is fiscally transparent under section 22 of the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112). The partnership does not file a standalone profits tax return; each partner is separately assessed on their share of Hong Kong-sourced partnership profits. The IRD assigns each partner a separate Taxpayer Reference Number (TRN) upon registration or upon filing of the partner's first Profits Tax Return.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Hong Kong does not operate a 'check-the-box' entity classification election or an elective transparency regime under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112). Partnerships are mandatorily treated as pass-through for profits tax purposes. No hybrid mismatch election is available. The IRD may apply the general anti-avoidance provisions in sections 61 and 61A of the IRO to disregard or recharacterize artificial transactions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No general VAT, GST, or sales and use tax is imposed in Hong Kong. The indirect tax regime is limited to specific duties on dutiable commodities under the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (Cap. 109), which do not apply to engineering CAD/BIM services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable - there is no VAT/GST/sales-tax registration threshold in Hong Kong because no broad-based indirect tax exists.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory e-invoicing pre-authorization, tax-API integration, or anti-fraud digital stamping regime exists under Hong Kong tax law. Electronic invoices and records have legal validity under the Electronic Transactions Ordinance (Cap. 553), and the IRD accepts electronically generated business records for tax purposes provided they are complete, accurate, and retained in accordance with the record-keeping obligations in the Inland Revenue Ordinance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable. Hong Kong does not levy VAT/GST, and therefore there is no 0% export rate, no statutory zero-rating mechanism, and no input tax credit or refund system for cross-border services. For profits tax purposes, income from cross-border engineering CAD/BIM services may be treated as outside the territorial scope of Hong Kong taxation if the services are performed and the contracts are negotiated and enforced outside Hong Kong, but this is a territorial-source analysis under section 14 of the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112), not an indirect-tax zero-rating claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable to indirect tax - Hong Kong imposes no VAT/GST and therefore requires no customs export declaration, bill of entry, bill of lading, or inward remittance certificate for zero-rated export VAT purposes. For profits tax territorial-source substantiation, the FIP should retain service contracts, invoices, bank statements, remittance confirmations, project work logs, and evidence that all service performance activities occurred outside Hong Kong.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Not applicable to VAT/GST export zero-rating because no indirect tax is levied. However, in a profits tax audit, if the IRD determines that partnership profits are Hong Kong-sourced rather than offshore-sourced, the partners become liable for profits tax on their respective shares. Incorrect returns and fraudulent or willful tax evasion are subject to penalties under sections 80 and 82A of the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112), including fines and additional tax of up to three times the amount undercharged, as well as imprisonment in serious cases. The FIP must therefore maintain full documentary evidence of offshore service delivery, contract execution, client communications, and foreign exchange receipts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC); State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE); Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) as the HK-side authorised institution supervisor.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is convertible on current account under IMF Article VIII, but strict capital-account controls are administered by SAFE. A Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) with a Hong Kong treasury overlay cannot freely move capital into or out of mainland China. Inbound capital is only compliant through a SAFE-registered FDI foreign-exchange capital account; once converted to RMB, the funds must be used for the FIP's normal operating purposes. Partner loan and equity contributions are subject to capacity and maturity covenants. Profit and partnership distributions require audited financial statements, full tax settlement proof, bank confirmation of capital verification, and a SAFE-compliant remittance application; the Hong Kong remittance leg may face additional bank sanctions screening and source-of-funds scrutiny. Current-account revenues from CAD/BIM outsourcing are generally convertible and may be retained in foreign currency or settled into RMB, but every receipt must be accompanied by the service contract, invoice, tax vouchers and bank submission to SAFE. Historically mandatory surrender ratios have been abolished, so the largest practical hurdle is documentary precision and the bank's discretionary risk appetite rather than an absolute conversion ceiling. Currency convertibility in practice is therefore conditional and flow-specific.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE trade-monitoring rules, export/current-account foreign-exchange receipts must be repatriated to the PRC and credited to a designated bank account within 180 days of the date the export/service obligation is completed and invoiced, unless an offshore retention account has been previously approved. Mandatory conversion ratios are currently set at 0% for normal trade; the FIP may elect to keep 100% of receipts in a foreign-currency settlement account or convert any portion to RMB at a licensed bank's spot rate. In cases of abrupt capital-flow pressure, SAFE may temporarily reintroduce a compulsory surrender ratio, and the published ratio must then be observed. For BIM/CAD services exports, the 'export' trigger is the acceptance certificate or milestone invoice rather than a customs declaration; the bank will treat missing evidence as an unfiled trade receivable and may block the account.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for FDI Capital (SAFE-registered Capital Foreign Exchange Account)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (CNY Demand Deposit)
Foreign Currency Settlement Account (USD/HKD/CNY) for Current-Account Receipts
HK Offshore Operating and RMB Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable as a core treasury rail. Offshore digital EMIs (including Wise) do not hold a mainland Chinese banking licence, are not SAFE-designated banks, and cannot open a capital foreign-exchange account for an FIP, accept FDI capital injections, perform SAFE trade- and capital-account reporting, or issue clean SWIFT corporate MT103 with proper purpose coding. Mainland banks will reject upstream/downstream payments that route through an unlicensed EMI because the sending institution is not a regulated bank and the underlying FX narratives are incomplete. For the Hong Kong ancillary vehicle, Wise may be used only for negligible administrative expenses outside the regulated capital/trade pipeline, subject to HKMA payment service provider rules; it cannot replace the authorised bank wire, LC, CIPS or documentary collection rails. Feasibility rating: Low (core flows), Incidental (HK-side petty expenses).
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Onshore PRC: mandatory physical attendance. The FIP's managing partner or statutory authorised signatory must attend the branch in person to execute the account-opening agreement, provide original identity/passport and FIP business licence, and complete dual-verification/audio-visual KYC. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted by SAFE-licensed banks for capital or RMB conversion accounts. HK side: remote onboarding is available but the HKMA-licensed bank still requires videoconference identity verification of at least one natural person director or UBO plus certified true copies of the partnership deed, register of members and board/partner resolutions; a consular-certified copy of identity documents can support, but cannot replace, the live interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership structure of the Foreign-Invested Partnership, particularly nominee or silent partners with more than 25% economic interest routed through Hong Kong limited partnerships and offshore trusts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised FIP partnership deed and all amendments; full beneficial owner schedule; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements for every 10%-plus holder; register of members; HK Companies Registry current information and certificate of good standing; audited financial statements for each corporate partner; sanctions/PEP screening results; bank reference letters from the partners' home banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance and operational mismatch between the FIP's declared BIM/CAD outsourcing revenues and the absence of local engineering capability or physical business infrastructure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement and premises photos or utility records; employee list with contracts, social insurance/MPF and payroll bank statements; project management software licences and collaboration records; BIM/CAD sample deliverables and milestone acceptance certificates; client confirmation letters; accountant's report on economic substance and headcount; timeline of staff onboarding relative to invoice dates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering indicators in cross-border service invoices, such as round-number settlements, invoice prices deviating materially from quoted rates, repeated MT103 payments outside contractual milestones, or mismatched FX purpose codes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master service agreements or statement of work with fee schedule; itemised tax-compliant invoices cross-referenced to project codes; payment schedule and bank MT103 records; acceptance and progress certificates; project cost build-up and fee benchmark study; auditor's work-in-progress and revenue recognition schedules; correspondence trails proving contract authenticity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP and government-linked end-user screening alerts because the civil-infrastructure CAD/BIM projects may involve state-controlled buyers, politically exposed persons or embargoed territories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full counterparty and beneficial owner screening report against UN, OFAC, EU, UK and domestic sanctions lists; PEP classification with source of wealth statement; end-user/end-use undertaking signed by the buyer; technical description of CAD/BIM deliverables (design files and engineering drawings, not controlled equipment or software); government tender award notice or contract with the infrastructure owner; explanation of any high-risk jurisdiction nexus.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route all inbound funding from the HK treasury vehicle to the FIP's designated SAFE capital foreign-exchange account via SWIFT MT103. The MT103 must show the remitter as the registered Hong Kong SAR partner or investor, the beneficiary as the exact FIP legal name, and in Field 70 a purpose statement referencing the SAFE cross-border transaction category for inbound direct investment paid-in capital; the receiving bank will map the corresponding BOP/FX purpose code in its SAFE reporting and cannot accept generic personal or investment notes. After funds clear, the bank verifies under the capital-cap account payment mechanism against the FIP's business licence, partnership deed and SAFE FDI registration; for RMB settlement, the FIP must submit the relevant contract, invoice, payroll list or purchase order. If the capital comes in CNY from Hong Kong, use the RMB clearing line via CIPS or the Hong Kong RMB clearing bank. Capital verification for the Chinese FIP is evidenced by the bank-issued confirmation letter, not only by an audit report.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 with full contract and invoice references in Field 70 for direct service payments, subcontractor fees, royalties and operating expenses. For large civil-infrastructure procurement, issue an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit through the FIP's Tier-1 bank (MT700/MT707) with the beneficiary's draft, shipment/performance documents, and insurance as required. Documentary collections (D/P and D/A) are acceptable for medium-risk suppliers or repeat vendors where LC cost is not justified. Cross-border RMB disbursements should be routed via CIPS; USD and HKD payments clear through CHIPS/Fedwire and HKCHATS respectively. Every disbursement must be pre-matched to the SAFE service-trade or goods-trade file, with tax-compliant invoice documentation and the correct FX purpose code; otherwise the bank will reject the instruction under SAFE real-trade review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CNY deliverable forward contracts with a SAFE-licensed bank, limited to genuine current or capital account exposure and supported by the underlying contract.

Offshore CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) restricted to the HK treasury overlay for hedging CNH risk where an onshore deliverable hedge cannot be established; no speculation and no cross-currency settlement onshore.
Cross-currency swaps permitted only for matched debt or capital flows, such as converting USD-denominated partner loans into RMB funding, subject to SAFE registration and bank treasury approval.
FX options and zero-cost collars are permissible for transaction hedging only; sale of uncovered options and leveraged speculative structures are prohibited.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Registration Renewal / Renewal of Business Registration Certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the certificate anniversary date; the Inland Revenue Department issues a renewal demand approximately one month before expiry and requires payment within the following 30 days of the expiry date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts an immediate late fee of HKD 300 (approximately USD 38); continued non-payment within three months may result in prosecution, a fine of up to HKD 5,000, and imprisonment for up to six months. Persistent failure to maintain a valid Business Registration Certificate may lead to cancellation of the active business registration and enforcement recovery of all overdue fees and penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the date of issue of the Profits Tax Return, unless an extension is granted by IRD based on the accounting date; partnership returns are issued in the annual filing cycle for the basis period ended on the partnership's financial year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts escalating fixed penalties beginning at HKD 1,200 and increasing to HKD 3,000 or more for prolonged default, plus potential prosecution. The IRD may raise best-of-judgment assessments and may impose additional tax up to 100% of the tax undercharged if the failure results in understated tax liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions (BIR56A)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 April each year, being one month after the end of the year of assessment on 31 March; the return reports remuneration, salaries, commission, bonuses, and pensions paid to all employees who are Hong Kong source income earners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing within the prescribed time subjects the partnership to fixed monetary penalties beginning at HKD 1,500; aggravated or repeated offences may attract penalties of up to HKD 5,000 per month and prosecution in the District Court, with further fines imposed by the Court.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified CPA audit is legally mandatory in Hong Kong when the entity cannot rely on the small private company audit exemption, namely when any of the following thresholds is exceeded: annual turnover above HKD 20,000,000 (approximately USD 2,564,000), total assets above HKD 10,000,000 (approximately USD 1,282,000), or headcount above 100 employees. For a Hong Kong Foreign-Invested Partnership, the Inland Revenue Department also requires audited financial statements to accompany the Partnership Profits Tax Return where gross income exceeds HKD 5,000,000 (approximately USD 641,000), where the partnership claims a tax loss, where non-resident partners are allocated Hong Kong profits, or where IRD issues a written notice requiring audited accounts. The audit must be performed by a certified public accountant registered with the Accounting and Financial Reporting Council and must comply with Hong Kong Standards on Auditing.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS); HKFRS for Private Entities; Hong Kong SME Financial Reporting Standard; IFRS where the ultimate parent reports under IFRS or where the partnership is part of an internationally active group.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not require a separate publicly filed annual UBO return for a partnership vehicle, but the partnership must maintain current beneficial ownership and partner identity records on site. Where the entity maintains a Significant Controllers Register, that register must be updated within 7 days of any change and confirmed as accurate on at least an annual basis. A transfer of partnership interest, or a shareholding transfer in any corporate partner, must be recorded in the relevant internal statutory register within 30 days of the change; if the vehicle is registered as a limited partnership, any change in partners, partner particulars, contributions, or registered address must be reported to the Companies Registry using Form LP2 within 14 days. Ongoing customer due diligence and ultimate beneficial ownership records must be refreshed at least annually or upon any material event under the Hong Kong Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Register of Partners and Contributions
Register of Directors / Register of General Partners

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800 to USD 6,000 per annum for a low-risk CAD/BIM partnership

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% standard Profits Tax rate for unincorporated businesses/partnerships; first HK$2,000,000 of assessable profits is taxed at 7.5% under the two-tiered regime
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial source tax system; offshore-source profits exempt from Profits Tax; no capital gains tax; no dividend withholding tax; enhanced research and development tax deduction of 200% on first HK$2 million and 300% on the excess for qualifying R&D expenditure; no VAT/GST in Hong Kong; tax losses carried forward for 5 years under the model specification (although Hong Kong statutory law generally permits indefinite carry-forward)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) Form BIR52 - Partnership Profits Tax Return; filed electronically via the IRD eTax e-Filing Portal (https://e-tax.ird.gov.hk)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within one calendar month from the date of issue of the return under s.64(1) of the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112); the Commissioner may grant extensions, generally to 15 August for accounting periods ending 31 December and to 15 November for accounting periods ending 31 March

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership legal name, Business Registration Number (BRN), registered office address, and correspondence details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the exact legal name as registered in Hong Kong; the BRN must match the Business Registration Office record. Non-resident partners must ensure the address is a substantive Hong Kong location, not a P.O. Box, because IRD will serve assessments and demands on the partnership address and also issue notices to each partner's tax representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Year of assessment and basis period, showing the accounting period ending within the year of assessment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a FIP with a 31 December fiscal year-end, the basis period is 1 January through 31 December. Non-resident partners must reconcile this Hong Kong basis period with their home-country tax filings to properly claim cross-border foreign tax credits; any mismatch in period is a common audit trigger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity code under the Hong Kong Standard Industrial Classification (HSIC v2.0)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the code corresponding to ISIC 7110 / NAICS 541330 for architectural and engineering activities, specifically Building Information Modeling (BIM) and structural drafting. Accurate coding is essential: misclassification as a general IT/BPO company will trigger a high-risk profile and transfer pricing documentation review for outsourcing entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover or gross proceeds derived from the partnership's trade, profession, or business
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only gross receipts from BIM/CAD services rendered to clients, including any intercompany billings to the China-related party. For non-resident partners, if the relevant contracts are both made and performed entirely outside Hong Kong, an offshore profits claim may be made in the attached schedule; however, the IRD will scrutinize the actual location of contract negotiation, approval, and performance, and will re-classify as Hong Kong-source income if any core decision-making is carried out in Hong Kong.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All allowable deductions claimed, including direct costs of CAD production, staff salaries, office rent, professional fees, depreciation, and other expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are allowed only under s.16 IRO if they are incurred in the production of assessable profits and are not of a capital nature. Payments made to related parties, especially the Chinese parent, must be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation satisfying the arm's-length principle; any deductible expense paid to a non-resident must be reported and may be re-characterized if the recipient has no commercial substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted assessable profit or adjusted loss before allocation to partners, after adding back non-deductible items and applying loss set-off rules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the partnership-level taxable figure. For a pass-through partnership, this amount is then apportioned among partners according to the partnership agreement. Non-resident corporate partners are taxed on their share at the corporate rate of 16.5% (8.25% on first HK$2 million apportioned on a pro-rata basis); non-resident individual partners are taxed at 15% (7.5% on first HK$2 million). If the partnership records an adjusted loss, the loss is allocated to partners and may be available to carry forward in each partner's own assessments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of assessable profits or losses to each partner, including a detailed schedule identifying resident and non-resident partners and their profit/loss sharing ratios
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the partner allocation schedule (BIR52 Sch. A/B) with full name, address, tax reference number, tax status (resident or non-resident, individual or corporation) and the agreed profit-sharing ratio. Every non-resident partner must appoint a Hong Kong tax agent or resident person under s.11(2) and s.76 IRO to receive service of notices. Failure to disclose non-resident partners, or use of a nominee, will render the partnership and the general partner jointly and severally liable for the unpaid Profits Tax of all partners.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or failure to file Form BIR52 may result in a fine of HK$10,000 under s.80(2) of the Inland Revenue Ordinance, together with imprisonment of up to 6 months; where the failure is committed with intent to evade tax, the penalty increases to three times the tax undercharged plus a fine of HK$50,000 under s.82A. Persistent failure may lead the Commissioner to issue an estimated assessment, and continued neglect can be remitted to the Court with fines of up to HK$200,000 and imprisonment of up to 1 year. Deliberate fraud involving diversion of funds through offshore accounts can trigger criminal prosecution under s.82A with a maximum term of imprisonment of 3 years and asset confiscation orders.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Hong Kong does not impose any withholding tax on dividends, including profit distributions by a partnership. The partnership itself is not taxed at entity level; profits are taxed in the hands of partners. Thus, repatriation of profits from Hong Kong to non-resident partners is generally free of dividend withholding tax, but the partners must file Profits Tax returns and pay tax at their applicable rate before distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Since Hong Kong does not impose a domestic withholding tax on dividends outbound, treaty relief for dividends is not typically necessary. For inbound payments (interest, royalties, or dividends received by the Hong Kong partnership from China), the taxpayer claiming benefits under the Mainland China - Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement (DTA) must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the IRD, typically by submitting Form IR1313A - Application for Certificate of Resident Person; (2) provide the TRC to the payer in China; (3) submit a beneficial ownership declaration confirming that the Hong Kong partnership is the ultimate beneficial owner and does not act as a conduit; (4) demonstrate substantive economic presence in Hong Kong through staff, office, and Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA); and (5) include a statement of eligibility under the relevant DTA article. For the China-Hong Kong Arrangement, the reduced withholding rate on dividends is 5% if the beneficial owner holds at least 25% of the paying company's capital, otherwise 10%; interest is capped at 7%; royalties are capped at 7%. The IRD will issue the TRC only after verifying the tax residence status and that the entity has sufficient economic substance to benefit from treaty protection.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Hong Kong does not levy a general withholding tax on interest paid to non-residents. However, royalties paid to a non-resident for the use of intellectual property in Hong Kong are deemed assessable profits under s.15(1)(a) and s.20B of the IRO. The deemed profit is 30% of the gross royalty, which results in an effective Hong Kong Profits Tax of 4.5% for an unincorporated partnership (30% deemed profit x 15% tax rate) or 4.95% if the non-resident partner is a corporation (30% x 16.5%). Under the China-Hong Kong DTA, the withholding limits are 7% for interest and 7% for royalties; if the royalty is for the use of industrial, commercial, or scientific equipment, the treaty rate may be reduced to 5% in some cases. To apply the DTA rate, the payer must obtain a TRC and beneficial ownership certificate, and the IRD may require the payer to withhold the excess and file a tentative tax return.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under DIPN 58 (Transfer Pricing Documentation), a Local File is required if the total amount of controlled transactions in any single category exceeds HK$4,000,000 for services, intangible property, or financial transactions, or exceeds HK$8,000,000 for goods purchases or sales. A Master File is required where the ultimate parent entity's group consolidated revenue exceeds HK$680,000,000 and the Hong Kong entity engages in controlled transactions with foreign related parties.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Hong Kong has not enacted dedicated Economic Substance Regulations similar to the BVI, Cayman, or UAE. However, the Inland Revenue Ordinance, in particular the General Anti-Abuse Rule under s.61A, the anti-treaty-shopping provision under s.9A, and DIPN 60 on offshore profits, impose functional and substance analysis. The partnership must demonstrate real and substantive economic activity in Hong Kong: a physical office, full-time employees with BIM/CAD expertise, local decision-making on contracts and pricing, and maintenance of key records. A partnership that merely invoices from Hong Kong while performing all Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in mainland China will fail the economic substance test; the IRD may recharacterize the profits as Hong Kong-source, impose penalties, and disallow treaty benefits under the BEPS multilateral instrument.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - False Offshore Profit Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Foreign-Invested Partnership claims 100% offshore-source profits exemption on all BIM/CAD service fees even though all strategic marketing, cost-allocation, personnel onboarding, and profit-negotiating decisions are made in Hong Kong, while operational staff and data-processing centers are in mainland China. The partnership is a paper vehicle with no Hong Kong office, no full-time employees, and no active management of contracts; a deliberate under-declaration of assessable profits is made to exploit Hong Kong's territorial tax system.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under s.82A of the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112), any person who knowingly and willfully makes a false return or neglects to report assessable profits is liable to a penalty of three times the tax undercharged, in addition to a fine of HK$50,000. Under s.80(2), conviction on indictment triggers a fine of HK$50,000 and imprisonment for up to 3 years; summary conviction carries a fine of HK$10,000 and imprisonment for 6 months. The Commissioner may also raise additional assessments for the statute-barred years if fraud is proven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner or managing partner of the FIP is personally and jointly severally liable for the partnership's tax liabilities under s.71 IRO. The doctrine of piercing the corporate veil applies where the partnership is used as a facade to avoid tax: the IRD may disregard the partnership structure and assess the controlling partners directly. Subject to forfeiture orders, the partners' personal bank accounts and other assets can be seized; the Commissioner may also seek a travel restriction (blacklisting) through the High Court, preventing departed directors or partners from leaving Hong Kong until tax and penalties are paid. In egregious criminal cases, the relevant partner faces imprisonment of up to 3 years, and under the Organized and Serious Crimes Ordinance, the court can impose a confiscation order equal to the benefit derived from tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing - Unjustified Cost-Plus Markup on Intercompany CAD Services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The FIP charges its mainland China parent for BIM drafting services at a fixed 3% cost-plus markup on total operating costs, regardless of the complexity, value, and risks assumed. The mark-up is not supported by any benchmarking study, and the FIP does not maintain a Local File or Master File even though its aggregate intra-group service revenue exceeds HK$4,000,000. This intercompany pricing fails the arm's-length principle and artificially shifts taxable profits from China (25% corporate income tax) to Hong Kong (15% or 16.5% profits tax), creating a disguised profit repatriation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The IRD has the authority under s.20AAA, s.50AAM, and s.50AAP of the IRO to adjust the income to reflect an arm's-length consideration. Upon adjustment, an additional assessment is raised with a penalty of up to 100% of the extra tax under s.82A. Moreover, failure to prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation as required by DIPN 58 incurs a fixed penalty of HK$50,000 under s.51D and an additional penalty for each day of continuing default. The China State Taxation Administration (STA) may also conduct a correlative adjustment and impose underpayment penalties at 25% punitive corporate tax plus late fee surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors (or general partners) who knowingly sign false TP documentation or approve non-arm's-length invoices are liable to personal penalties under the IRO; the IRD can pierce the partnership to recover the additional tax and penalty directly from directors' personal assets. In fraudulent trading scenarios, the Companies Ordinance s.458 may impose criminal liability on directors who participate in business carried on with intent to defraud creditors, with a maximum imprisonment of 15 years and unlimited fines. The IRD also shares information with the China tax authorities under the bilateral exchange of information; a trans-border transfer pricing investigation can result in double tax consequences, blacklisting of the directors in both jurisdictions, and criminal prosecution for making false written representations to tax authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Shell Company - Economic Substance Deficiency and Money Laundering Through Trade Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The FIP is organized as a Hong Kong registered limited partnership with no operating premises, no Hong Kong employees, no bank account in Hong Kong held for payroll, and no visible business correspondence. The partnership receives monthly wire payments from a mainland China government-related engineering conglomerate for CAD/BIM outsourcing; the funds are transferred immediately (within 2 hours) to an offshore beneficiary in the British Virgin Islands. The transaction flow is designed with no commercial rationale other than to convert mainland Chinese payments into offshore tax-privileged cash while avoiding HK Profits Tax and circumventing China's capital control regulations. Such invoicing and payment arrangement constitutes the use of a shell partnership for tax evasion and money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The IRD may treat the partnership as a sham under s.61A of the IRO and disregard all transactions, assessing the Chinese resident partner as if the income had been received directly in China. The Financial Intelligence Office and the Commercial Crime Bureau may impose penalties under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615) with fines of up to HK$5,000,000 and imprisonment of up to 7 years for non-compliance with AML due diligence and record-keeping requirements. The court may also impose a control order under the Prevention of Bribery and Corruption Ordinance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: For limited partnerships, the limited partners have capital protection only if they refrain from participating in management; the general partner who establishes and controls the shell FIP is personally liable for all tax debts, penalties, and legal costs. Piercing the corporate veil is automatic because a partnership is not a separate legal person in Hong Kong; creditors and the tax authority can execute directly against the general partner's personal estate. In laundering proceedings under the Drug Trafficking and Organized Crime Ordinance, the general partner may be sentenced to life imprisonment and fined HK$5,000,000; a confiscation order covers the full amount of the laundered payments, and the partner's Hong Kong property, accounts, and passport can be frozen and revoked.
